content: 述情障碍与医护人员COVID-19疫苗接种后体液免疫降低独立相关:一项不受失眠及代谢因素影响的首次证据 《Metabolism Open》:First Evidence of an Association Between Alexithymia and Reduced Humoral Immunity Following COVID-19 Vaccination, Independent of Insomnia and Metabolic Factors in Healthcare Workers 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月25日 来源:Metabolism Open 3.5 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 本研究首次探讨述情障碍(alexithymia)是否与医护人员接种BNT162b2 mRNA疫苗后的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2型(SARS-CoV-2)抗刺突蛋白(anti-S)免疫球蛋白G(IgG)抗体浓度独立相关。研究纳入198名来自希腊两家三级公立医院的医护人员,于最后一剂疫苗接种后4–6个月采集空腹血样,采用化学发光微粒子免疫分析法(CMIA)定量检测anti-S IgG抗体浓度,并使用多伦多述情障碍量表(TAS-20)、雅典失眠量表(AIS)、汉密尔顿焦虑量表(HAM-A)及汉密尔顿抑郁量表(HAM-D)进行心理测评。多变量线性回归分析显示,在调整人口学、代谢及炎症协变量后,述情障碍(TAS-20评分)与anti-S IgG浓度呈显著独立负相关(fold-change 0.98,95% CI 0.96–1.00,p = 0.002),失眠(AIS评分)亦为抗体水平的独立负向决定因素(fold-change 0.90,95% CI 0.86–0.95,p < 0.001)。按既往感染史分层后,上述关联在未感染及既往感染亚组中均保持显著。以代谢胰岛素抵抗评分(METS-IR)替代体质指数(BMI)进行敏感性分析时,结果保持一致。此外,发热等疫苗相关不良事件与较高抗体滴度及较低述情障碍评分相关。研究人员得出结论:述情障碍与失眠是BNT162b2疫苗接种后体液免疫反应的独立负向预测因素,提示心身特质可能通过神经内分泌-免疫通路影响疫苗诱导的抗体应答,为优化高风险人群的疫苗免疫策略提供了潜在干预靶点。 **研究背景与问题** 欢迎领取“抗体偶联药物前沿研发方案” 领 取 全球范围内严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2型(SARS-CoV-2)疫苗的广泛接种在控制新型冠状病毒病(COVID-19)大流行中发挥了关键作用,其中BNT162b2 mRNA疫苗在预防重症和降低死亡率方面显示出高效力。然而,疫苗诱导的体液免疫强度存在显著个体间差异,既往研究已识别出多种生物学、代谢、行为及心理决定因素,包括疫苗剂量数、混合免疫、宿主遗传、年龄、性别、慢性合并症、肥胖及胰岛素抵抗等代谢健康参数,以及营养状态和生活方式因素。心理特征对免疫功能的调节作用日益受到关注,心理压力、睡眠紊乱、焦虑和抑郁症状已被证实与多种传染病背景下的免疫应答受损及疫苗效力降低相关。然而,述情障碍(alexithymia)——一种以难以识别和描述情绪及外向性思维为特征的心身人格特质——在疫苗接种研究领域尚未得到系统关注。述情障碍与免疫失调的关联已有累积证据,包括白细胞介素(IL)-2和IL-4产生减少、CD4+百分比降低、Th1/Th2比值改变以及慢性交感激活和糖皮质激素分泌增加等神经内分泌变化,这些均可能损害细胞介导的免疫。尽管存在上述观察,述情障碍在塑造疫苗诱导免疫应答(尤其是SARS-CoV-2疫苗接种后)中的潜在作用尚未被系统研究。医护人员作为承受持续职业压力、睡眠中断和昼夜节律负荷的群体,其心身特质与免疫应答的交互作用尤为值得关注。本研究首次在医护人员中探讨述情障碍是否与BNT162b2疫苗接种后的抗刺突蛋白(anti-S)免疫球蛋白G(IgG)抗体浓度独立相关,同时综合评估失眠、焦虑、抑郁症状及积极思维等心理因素的独立作用。 **研究方法概述** 本研究为横断面研究,纳入来自希腊雅典“G. Gennimatas”综合医院和特里波利斯综合Arcadian医院的198名医护人员,均接受过两剂或三剂BNT162b2 mRNA疫苗(COMIRNATY?,辉瑞- BioNTech)。排除标准包括免疫功能低下状态、自身免疫或风湿性疾病、恶性肿瘤、慢性肝肾血液或心血管疾病、使用抗抑郁或抗焦虑药物以及疫苗接种程序启动前有记录的COVID-19感染。于最后一剂疫苗接种后4–6个月采集空腹血样,采用SARS-CoV-2 IgG II Quant检测(雅培实验室)化学发光微粒子免疫分析法(CMIA)定量检测anti-S IgG抗体浓度。心理测评采用20项多伦多述情障碍量表(TAS-20)(总分≥61判定述情障碍存在)、14项汉密尔顿焦虑量表(HAM-A)、17项汉密尔顿抑郁量表(HAM-D)及雅典失眠量表(AIS)(≥6分判定临床显著失眠)。积极思维采用单项自评问题评估。统计方法包括Mann–Whitney U检验、Kruskal–Wallis检验、Spearman等级相关分析及以log转换anti-S IgG为因变量的多变量线性回归模型,回归系数经反变换以倍数变化(fold-change)及95%置信区间(CI)表示。 **主要研究结果** **研究人群特征与抗体水平** 198名医护人员中,平均年龄47.7±11.6岁,73.7%为女性,平均体质指数(BMI)为25.9±4.4 kg/m2。35.4%的参与者符合述情障碍标准(TAS-20≥61),52.5%在抗体评估前有记录的COVID-19感染史。疫苗诱导的anti-S IgG几何平均滴度为6,373.4 AU/mL(95% CI 5,190–7,820)。82.3%的参与者报告了疫苗相关不良事件,注射部位压痛(61.6%)、肌痛(45.5%)和疲劳(41.4%)最为常见。 **单因素分析结果** 单因素分析显示,接受三剂疫苗者抗体滴度显著高于两剂者(8,455.8对5,239.4 AU/mL,p = 0.002);有既往感染史者抗体水平显著更高(11,077.7对4,886.5 AU/mL,p < 0.001)。当前吸烟者的抗体水平低于不吸烟者和既往吸烟者(p < 0.001)。夜班工作与较低的anti-S IgG滴度相关(p = 0.036)。自报经常积极思维者的抗体水平显著高于罕有积极思维者(11,585.2对6,618.6 AU/mL,p = 0.015)。 **心理量表相关分析** Spearman相关分析显示,TAS-20评分与HAM-A(r = 0.204,p = 0.004)、HAM-D(r = 0.145,p = 0.042)及AIS评分(r = 0.180,p = 0.011)呈正相关。IgG水平与AIS(r = ?0.474,p < 0.001)、HAM-A(r = ?0.416,p < 0.001)、HAM-D(r = ?0.222,p = 0.002)、TAS-20(r = ?0.297,p < 0.001)、DIF(r = ?0.410,p < 0.001)和DDF(r = ?0.246,p < 0.001)均呈显著负相关,同时与hsCRP(r = ?0.141,p = 0.048)及IL-6(r = ?0.240,p < 0.001)亦呈负相关。EOT亚量表与抗体水平无显著相关。 **多变量回归分析结果** 以log转换anti-S IgG为因变量的多变量线性回归分析(逐步法)显示:既往COVID-19感染(p < 0.001)、接受三剂疫苗(p = 0.007)和较高BMI(p = 0.011)为抗体水平的显著正独立相关因素;而AIS评分(p < 0.001)、IL-6(p < 0.001)、TAS-20评分(p = 0.002)和当前吸烟(p = 0.020)为负向独立相关因素。较低酒精摄入与较高抗体水平相关(p = 0.002)。最终模型解释的方差比例较高(调整后R2 = 0.46)。 **分层分析结果** 在未感染亚组中,第三剂疫苗与较高anti-S IgG独立相关(fold-change 1.48,95% CI 1.14–1.92,p = 0.004),AIS、TAS-20和IL-6与较低抗体滴度独立相关。在既往感染亚组中,AIS(fold-change 0.90,95% CI 0.86–0.95,p < 0.001)和TAS-20(fold-change 0.98,95% CI 0.97–0.99,p = 0.001)仍为显著负向决定因素,BMI(fold-change 1.03,95% CI 1.01–1.06,p = 0.017)和较低酒精摄入为正向相关因素。以METS-IR替代BMI进行敏感性分析后,述情障碍与失眠的独立负向关联保持一致。 **不良事件与心理因素分析** 报告疫苗相关不良事件的参与者较无不良事件者具有更高的anti-S IgG滴度(8,661.0对5,477.4 AU/mL,p = 0.003)。发热是与较高抗体水平关联最强的症状(27,763.1对4,886.5 AU/mL,p < 0.001),肌痛(p = 0.005)和寒战(p = 0.031)也与较高滴度相关。报告不良事件者的心理困扰评分(AIS、HAM-A、HAM-D)更高,而发热与较低TAS-20评分(53对57,p < 0.001)及较低的AIS、HAM-A、HAM-D评分相关。 **讨论与结论** 本研究首次提供述情障碍与BNT162b2疫苗接种后anti-S IgG浓度降低独立相关的证据,且该关联在调整人口学、代谢和炎症协变量后仍保持显著,并在感染分层分析中一致存在。这一发现与述情障碍相关的免疫失调机制相符——述情障碍个体表现出IL-2和IL-4产生减少、CD4+百分比降低以及Th1/Th2比值偏向Th2主导的免疫状态,这些改变归因于述情障碍特征性的慢性交感激活和糖皮质激素分泌升高。值得注意的是,DIF和DDF亚量表与较低抗体水平的显著相关性而EOT无此关联,提示述情障碍的情感成分(而非认知成分)可能是连接述情障碍与免疫失调的关键心理生物学通路。 失眠与抗体水平的强负相关与睡眠紊乱损害疫苗免疫原性的累积证据一致。睡眠剥夺扰乱生长激素和催乳素的夜间释放同时增加皮质醇分泌,从而损害Th1/Th2细胞因子平衡并降低抗原呈递细胞功能。夜班工作在单因素分析中与较低抗体滴度相关但在多变量模型中未保持显著,可能反映了与失眠的共享方差,提示失眠可能部分介导昼夜节律紊乱-免疫通路。 焦虑和抑郁症状在单因素分析中与抗体水平相关但未在多变量模型中保持显著,可能与述情障碍和失眠捕获了本应归因于焦虑和抑郁的方差有关。自报经常积极思维与较高抗体水平的单因素关联支持积极情感增强疫苗免疫原性的证据,但该关联未在多变量模型中保持显著。 研究局限性包括横断面设计无法推断因果关系、抗体滴度仅在单一时间点(接种后4–6个月)测量、积极思维采用单项自评工具缺乏验证、未测量中和活性及细胞免疫以及研究人群的选择性。研究结论为:述情障碍和失眠是BNT162b2疫苗接种后医护人员anti-S IgG浓度的独立负向相关因素,即使在校正人口学、代谢和炎症协变量后仍保持显著。这些发现将心理神经免疫学文献延伸至疫苗诱导免疫领域,提示心身特质可能有助于解释疫苗接种后体液免疫应答的个体间差异。鉴于述情障碍和失眠均可通过针对性干预加以改善,这些结果可能对优化高风险人群的疫苗应答具有潜在意义。未来前瞻性纵向研究应考察旨在提升情绪觉察和睡眠质量的干预措施是否能够增强疫苗诱导的免疫。 **研究背景与问题**全球范围内严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2型(SARS-CoV-2)疫苗的广泛接种在控制新型冠状病毒病(COVID-19)大流行中发挥了关键作用,其中BNT162b2 mRNA疫苗在预防重症和降低死亡率方面显示出高效力。然而,疫苗诱导的体液免疫强度存在显著个体间差异,既往研究已识别出多种生物学、代谢、行为及心理决定因素,包括疫苗剂量数、混合免疫、宿主遗传、年龄、性别、慢性合并症、肥胖及胰岛素抵抗等代谢健康参数,以及营养状态和生活方式因素。心理特征对免疫功能的调节作用日益受到关注,心理压力、睡眠紊乱、焦虑和抑郁症状已被证实与多种传染病背景下的免疫应答受损及疫苗效力降低相关。然而,述情障碍(alexithymia)——一种以难以识别和描述情绪及外向性思维为特征的心身人格特质——在疫苗接种研究领域尚未得到系统关注。述情障碍与免疫失调的关联已有累积证据,包括白细胞介素(IL)-2和IL-4产生减少、CD4百分比降低、Th1/Th2比值改变以及慢性交感激活和糖皮质激素分泌增加等神经内分泌变化,这些均可能损害细胞介导的免疫。尽管存在上述观察,述情障碍在塑造疫苗诱导免疫应答(尤其是SARS-CoV-2疫苗接种后)中的潜在作用尚未被系统研究。医护人员作为承受持续职业压力、睡眠中断和昼夜节律负荷的群体,其心身特质与免疫应答的交互作用尤为值得关注。本研究首次在医护人员中探讨述情障碍是否与BNT162b2疫苗接种后的抗刺突蛋白(anti-S)免疫球蛋白G(IgG)抗体浓度独立相关,同时综合评估失眠、焦虑、抑郁症状及积极思维等心理因素的独立作用。**研究方法概述**本研究为横断面研究,纳入来自希腊雅典“G. Gennimatas”综合医院和特里波利斯综合Arcadian医院的198名医护人员,均接受过两剂或三剂BNT162b2 mRNA疫苗(COMIRNATY?,辉瑞- BioNTech)。排除标准包括免疫功能低下状态、自身免疫或风湿性疾病、恶性肿瘤、慢性肝肾血液或心血管疾病、使用抗抑郁或抗焦虑药物以及疫苗接种程序启动前有记录的COVID-19感染。于最后一剂疫苗接种后4–6个月采集空腹血样,采用SARS-CoV-2 IgG II Quant检测(雅培实验室)化学发光微粒子免疫分析法(CMIA)定量检测anti-S IgG抗体浓度。心理测评采用20项多伦多述情障碍量表(TAS-20)(总分≥61判定述情障碍存在)、14项汉密尔顿焦虑量表(HAM-A)、17项汉密尔顿抑郁量表(HAM-D)及雅典失眠量表(AIS)(≥6分判定临床显著失眠)。积极思维采用单项自评问题评估。统计方法包括Mann–Whitney U检验、Kruskal–Wallis检验、Spearman等级相关分析及以log转换anti-S IgG为因变量的多变量线性回归模型,回归系数经反变换以倍数变化(fold-change)及95%置信区间(CI)表示。**主要研究结果****研究人群特征与抗体水平**198名医护人员中,平均年龄47.7±11.6岁,73.7%为女性,平均体质指数(BMI)为25.9±4.4 kg/m2。35.4%的参与者符合述情障碍标准(TAS-20≥61),52.5%在抗体评估前有记录的COVID-19感染史。疫苗诱导的anti-S IgG几何平均滴度为6,373.4 AU/mL(95% CI 5,190–7,820)。82.3%的参与者报告了疫苗相关不良事件,注射部位压痛(61.6%)、肌痛(45.5%)和疲劳(41.4%)最为常见。**单因素分析结果**单因素分析显示,接受三剂疫苗者抗体滴度显著高于两剂者(8,455.8对5,239.4 AU/mL,p = 0.002);有既往感染史者抗体水平显著更高(11,077.7对4,886.5 AU/mL,p < 0.001)。当前吸烟者的抗体水平低于不吸烟者和既往吸烟者(p < 0.001)。夜班工作与较低的anti-S IgG滴度相关(p = 0.036)。自报经常积极思维者的抗体水平显著高于罕有积极思维者(11,585.2对6,618.6 AU/mL,p = 0.015)。**心理量表相关分析**Spearman相关分析显示,TAS-20评分与HAM-A(r = 0.204,p = 0.004)、HAM-D(r = 0.145,p = 0.042)及AIS评分(r = 0.180,p = 0.011)呈正相关。IgG水平与AIS(r = ?0.474,p < 0.001)、HAM-A(r = ?0.416,p < 0.001)、HAM-D(r = ?0.222,p = 0.002)、TAS-20(r = ?0.297,p < 0.001)、DIF(r = ?0.410,p < 0.001)和DDF(r = ?0.246,p < 0.001)均呈显著负相关,同时与hsCRP(r = ?0.141,p = 0.048)及IL-6(r = ?0.240,p < 0.001)亦呈负相关。EOT亚量表与抗体水平无显著相关。**多变量回归分析结果**以log转换anti-S IgG为因变量的多变量线性回归分析(逐步法)显示:既往COVID-19感染(p < 0.001)、接受三剂疫苗(p = 0.007)和较高BMI(p = 0.011)为抗体水平的显著正独立相关因素;而AIS评分(p < 0.001)、IL-6(p < 0.001)、TAS-20评分(p = 0.002)和当前吸烟(p = 0.020)为负向独立相关因素。较低酒精摄入与较高抗体水平相关(p = 0.002)。最终模型解释的方差比例较高(调整后R2 = 0.46)。**分层分析结果**在未感染亚组中,第三剂疫苗与较高anti-S IgG独立相关(fold-change 1.48,95% CI 1.14–1.92,p = 0.004),AIS、TAS-20和IL-6与较低抗体滴度独立相关。在既往感染亚组中,AIS(fold-change 0.90,95% CI 0.86–0.95,p < 0.001)和TAS-20(fold-change 0.98,95% CI 0.97–0.99,p = 0.001)仍为显著负向决定因素,BMI(fold-change 1.03,95% CI 1.01–1.06,p = 0.017)和较低酒精摄入为正向相关因素。以METS-IR替代BMI进行敏感性分析后,述情障碍与失眠的独立负向关联保持一致。**不良事件与心理因素分析**报告疫苗相关不良事件的参与者较无不良事件者具有更高的anti-S IgG滴度(8,661.0对5,477.4 AU/mL,p = 0.003)。发热是与较高抗体水平关联最强的症状(27,763.1对4,886.5 AU/mL,p < 0.001),肌痛(p = 0.005)和寒战(p = 0.031)也与较高滴度相关。报告不良事件者的心理困扰评分(AIS、HAM-A、HAM-D)更高,而发热与较低TAS-20评分(53对57,p < 0.001)及较低的AIS、HAM-A、HAM-D评分相关。**讨论与结论**本研究首次提供述情障碍与BNT162b2疫苗接种后anti-S IgG浓度降低独立相关的证据,且该关联在调整人口学、代谢和炎症协变量后仍保持显著,并在感染分层分析中一致存在。这一发现与述情障碍相关的免疫失调机制相符——述情障碍个体表现出IL-2和IL-4产生减少、CD4百分比降低以及Th1/Th2比值偏向Th2主导的免疫状态,这些改变归因于述情障碍特征性的慢性交感激活和糖皮质激素分泌升高。值得注意的是,DIF和DDF亚量表与较低抗体水平的显著相关性而EOT无此关联,提示述情障碍的情感成分(而非认知成分)可能是连接述情障碍与免疫失调的关键心理生物学通路。失眠与抗体水平的强负相关与睡眠紊乱损害疫苗免疫原性的累积证据一致。睡眠剥夺扰乱生长激素和催乳素的夜间释放同时增加皮质醇分泌,从而损害Th1/Th2细胞因子平衡并降低抗原呈递细胞功能。夜班工作在单因素分析中与较低抗体滴度相关但在多变量模型中未保持显著,可能反映了与失眠的共享方差,提示失眠可能部分介导昼夜节律紊乱-免疫通路。焦虑和抑郁症状在单因素分析中与抗体水平相关但未在多变量模型中保持显著,可能与述情障碍和失眠捕获了本应归因于焦虑和抑郁的方差有关。自报经常积极思维与较高抗体水平的单因素关联支持积极情感增强疫苗免疫原性的证据,但该关联未在多变量模型中保持显著。研究局限性包括横断面设计无法推断因果关系、抗体滴度仅在单一时间点(接种后4–6个月)测量、积极思维采用单项自评工具缺乏验证、未测量中和活性及细胞免疫以及研究人群的选择性。研究结论为:述情障碍和失眠是BNT162b2疫苗接种后医护人员anti-S IgG浓度的独立负向相关因素,即使在校正人口学、代谢和炎症协变量后仍保持显著。这些发现将心理神经免疫学文献延伸至疫苗诱导免疫领域,提示心身特质可能有助于解释疫苗接种后体液免疫应答的个体间差异。鉴于述情障碍和失眠均可通过针对性干预加以改善,这些结果可能对优化高风险人群的疫苗应答具有潜在意义。未来前瞻性纵向研究应考察旨在提升情绪觉察和睡眠质量的干预措施是否能够增强疫苗诱导的免疫。 打赏 展开全文 content: 伊朗设拉子蟑螂体表SARS-CoV-2 RNA分子检出及其机械携带潜能:经卵传播未检出的RT-PCR证据 《Parasite Epidemiology and Control》:Molecular evidence of SARS-CoV-2 detection on cockroaches in shiraz, southwestern Iran and potential implications for mechanical carriage 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月24日 来源:Parasite Epidemiology and Control 2.4 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 本研究探讨蟑螂体表是否可携带严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)RNA(核糖核酸),但未证实感染性传播。在经分子学分析的蟑螂体表中,29.5%检出SARS-CoV-2 RNA,医院污水中相对检出率最高(70%)。尽管存在体表污染,若虫(nymphs)或卵荚(egg capsules)中均未检出病毒RNA。蟑螂体表SARS-CoV-2 RNA检出提示其可能作为机械携带者(mechanical carrier),但传播仍未获确认。研究采用逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)检测蟑螂体表和组织中的SARS-CoV-2 RNA,提供了稳健的分子学评估。本研究有助于理解SARS-CoV-2的非人传播途径,并强调环境因素在病毒传播中的作用。 研究背景与问题。蟑螂(cockroaches)在人类环境中广泛分布,可携带细菌、病毒和寄生虫,并因取食、反吐和排泄等行为污染食物与表面,被视为重要机械携带者(mechanical carriage)。SARS-CoV-2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)主要经呼吸道飞沫和密切接触传播,但病毒可在环境表面持续存在,促使研究人员关注非人传播途径。蟑螂常出入医院、宿舍和食品制备区等可能被污染的环境,其体表与消化道均可能接触病原,因此需评估其是否可携带SARS-CoV-2 RNA(核糖核酸)。作者Maryam Motevasel、Mozafar Vahedi、Marzeyeh Jamalidost与Mohsen Kalantari指出,既往伊朗研究多限于医院,未纳入宿舍/教育机构,未评估若虫(nymphs)和卵荚(egg capsules)中的经卵传播(transovarial transmission),也未比较德国小蠊(Blattella germanica,B. germanica)与美洲大蠊(Periplaneta americana,P. americana)的病毒载量,故开展本研究。 Chromium X将单细胞研究提升至新台阶,欢迎深入了解10X Genomics单细胞多组学分析技术资料>> 领 取 研究设计与主要结论。研究人员在伊朗设拉子(Shiraz)开展横断面研究,采集400只蟑螂,其中200只用于SARS-CoV-2 RNA分子检测,另200只用于昆虫饲养垂直传播实验;检测体表与胃肠道组织,并观察若虫和卵荚。结果显示,体表SARS-CoV-2 RNA总检出率为29.5%,医院来源P. americana达70%,宿舍来源B. germanica达48%,教育机构标本未检出;内部组织检出率显著低于体表,且所有内部阳性均见于体表阳性标本;若虫与卵荚均未检出病毒RNA。多因素分析显示采集地点是检出的最强独立预测因素。研究结论支持蟑螂可作为SARS-CoV-2 RNA的机械携带者,但未支持其作为生物媒介(biological vector),亦未证实感染性传播;研究意义在于补充非人传播途径与环境因素证据,并提示医院、宿舍和污水系统等重点环境需加强卫生与虫害控制。 关键技术方法(不超过250字)。研究人员在设拉子Ali Asghar Hospital、Shahid Dastgheib dormitory、Paramedical School和School of Public Health采集蟑螂;2022年两个月共采集400只,随机取200只进行分子检测,另200只用于昆虫饲养垂直传播实验,并按RT-PCR状态分为阳性成体59只与阴性成体141只,观察若虫200只和卵荚50只。方法包括形态学鉴定、体表洗脱与胃肠道组织分离、两阶段池化筛查及阳性池解卷积、RNA提取、多重TaqMan RT-PCR同时检测SARS-CoV-2 RdRp与N基因及人RNase P内参(循环阈值Ct<38.0且双靶标阳性判为阳性),并采用卡方/Fisher、McNemar、t/Wilcoxon及logistic回归分析。 研究结果。3.1 Detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA(SARS-CoV-2 RNA的检出)。通过200只标本的体表洗脱与RT-PCR分析,研究人员在59/200只(29.5%;95% CI:23.4%–36.3%)蟑螂体表检出SARS-CoV-2 RNA;Shahid Dastgheib dormitory的B. germanica为24/50(48%;95% CI:34.2%–62.2%),Ali Asghar Hospital的P. americana为35/50(70%;95% CI:55.9%–81.2%),Paramedical School与School of Public Health合计0/100;医院与宿舍检出率差异显著(χ2=5.01,df=1,p=0.025;OR=2.53,95% CI:1.12–5.73),P. americana总体检出率高于B. germanica(35.0% vs 24.0%;χ2=4.57,df=1,p=0.032;OR=1.56,95% CI:1.04–2.34)。通过胃肠道组织分离与RT-PCR,内部组织检出11/59只体表阳性标本(18.6%;占总分析标本5.5%),未发现仅内部阳性者;体表与内部检出差异显著(McNemar检验,χ2=38.5,df=1,p<0.001)。体表平均Ct为29.8±1.6,内部为34.6±1.4(配对t检验,p<0.001);体表平均病毒载量为2820±620 copies/mL,内部为185±45 copies/mL(Wilcoxon检验,p<0.001),表面/内部载量比约15.2:1。B. germanica内部检出6/24(25%),P. americana为5/35(14.3%),种间内部检出率差异不显著(Fisher精确检验,p=0.322;OR=0.50,95% CI:0.12–2.03),但B. germanica内部载量210±55 copies/mL高于P. americana的155±38 copies/mL(独立t检验,p=0.048)。通过昆虫饲养与子代检测,200只若虫(来自阳性与阴性成体各100只)和50个卵荚(阳性与阴性成体各25个)均未检出病毒RNA。通过二元logistic回归,采集地点为最强独立预测因素(医院:OR=8.21,95% CI:4.52–14.92,p<0.001;宿舍:OR=4.31,95% CI:2.23–8.34,p<0.001;以教育机构为参照),物种在校正地点后非独立预测因素(校正OR=1.23,95% CI:0.78–1.94,p=0.376),模型拟合良好(Hosmer-Lemeshow检验,p=0.682)。污水来源P. americana体表载量3480±620 copies/mL高于室内B. germanica的2150±450 copies/mL(独立t检验,p<0.001)。 讨论与结论。讨论部分强调,RT-PCR检出病毒RNA不等于检出感染性病毒;内部病毒载量低且若虫、卵荚无RNA,符合机械携带而非生物传播,但因未进行细胞培养或亚基因组RNA等复制实验,不能断言蟑螂体内不发生病毒复制。作者认为,高体表污染、低内部携带的模式支持内部RNA主要源于摄入污染物质;蟑螂更可能是机械携带者而非生物媒介。讨论还指出,蟑螂在污染表面活动可潜在参与污染物传播,医院、宿舍和污水系统等重点环境应加强卫生与害虫控制;局限性包括单城市、两个月采样、池化筛查、亚组样本量有限、昆虫饲养条件不能完全模拟自然环境、未进行测序确认、未评估病毒存活与转移效率、未评估水平传播及未开展病毒活力实验。研究结论部分译文:本研究提供证据表明,蟑螂可在其外表面携带SARS-CoV-2 RNA,医院污水系统中P. americana检出率(35/50,70%;95% CI:55.9%–81.2%)显著高于宿舍厨房中B. germanica(24/50,48%;95% CI:34.2%–62.2%;χ2=5.01,df=1,p=0.025);多因素分析显示采集地点是检出的最强独立预测因素(医院:校正OR=8.21,95% CI:4.52–14.92,p<0.001),强调环境暴露在病毒RNA携带中的重要性。低内部病毒载量及若虫和卵荚中无RNA,符合机械携带而非生物传播;但由于未进行直接复制实验,不能断定蟑螂体内不发生病毒复制。关键局限是RT-PCR检测病毒RNA而非感染性病毒,因此不能得出蟑螂传播有活力SARS-CoV-2的结论。与既往报告相比,本研究证明未检出垂直传播并量化了物种和环境间RNA携带差异。这些发现确认蟑螂可能作为病毒RNA的机械携带者而非生物媒介,并强调高风险环境中有针对性卫生措施的必要性;未来需结合病毒活力实验以确定蟑螂机械传播感染性SARS-CoV-2是否可能。所有200只若虫和50个卵荚无病毒RNA,表明实验条件下未检出垂直传播,提示蟑螂种群不太可能通过经卵传播成为病毒储存库;内部RNA仅在体表阳性标本中检出,表面与内部平均病毒载量比约15:1,提供定量证据表明内部存在源于摄入污染物质而非主动感染或复制,这种高体表污染而低内部携带的模式是机械传播而非生物传播的特征。 研究背景与问题。蟑螂(cockroaches)在人类环境中广泛分布,可携带细菌、病毒和寄生虫,并因取食、反吐和排泄等行为污染食物与表面,被视为重要机械携带者(mechanical carriage)。SARS-CoV-2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)主要经呼吸道飞沫和密切接触传播,但病毒可在环境表面持续存在,促使研究人员关注非人传播途径。蟑螂常出入医院、宿舍和食品制备区等可能被污染的环境,其体表与消化道均可能接触病原,因此需评估其是否可携带SARS-CoV-2 RNA(核糖核酸)。作者Maryam Motevasel、Mozafar Vahedi、Marzeyeh content: Skip to content Show You CareStudent of the MonthEveryday FamiliesWorking IowaMemorialsAdvertise With UsCollette ToursSurprise SquadAging Untold 75° Cedar Rapids, IA Watch Live Streaming Studio News Weather Video Sports OnIowa Live KCRG 9.2 Everyday Iowa We the People Connect YouNews Home News Everyday Iowa Iowa National I9 Investigations Our Town Working Iowa Watch Live Streaming Studio First Alert Weather Radar Weather Now CityCAM StormNet Map Room Winter Severe Weather Cancellations Weather Kids Weather Academy Rivers Sports Hawkeyes Cyclones Panthers Athlete Of The Week Big Ol' Fish Scoreboard Latest Videos OnIowa Live KCRG 9.2 Everyday Iowa Aging Untold Contact Us Meet the Team Advertise With Us Submit a News Story Community Calendar Jobs at KCRG KCRG-TV9 Daily Digest TV Listings Show You Care Calendar Surprise Squad Wagner Tails Election Results Presidential Election Map Iowa Interactive Results Everyday Families YouNews Student of the Month Contests Surprise Squad Star-Spangled Sing-Off NextGen TV Job Connection Circle Country Local News Live PowerNation InvestigateTV Watching Your Wallet Digital Marketing Gray AI Policy COVID-19 vaccine mandate did not violate nursing student’s civil rights, Iowa Supreme Court rules The Court held it was the parents, not the student, who held religious beliefs against the vaccine By KCRG Staff Published: Oct. 23, 2026 at 2:24 PM UTC Share Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google CEDAR RAPIDS, Iowa (KCRG) - The Iowa Supreme Court upheld a ruling that a mandate for a nursing student to get the COVID-19 vaccine does not amount to religious discrimination because it was the parents, not the student, who held the religious conviction. The case stems from 2021, when Andrew Perry, a nursing student at the time at Dordt University in Sioux Center, sought a religious exemption from a COVID-19 vaccination requirement. The school did not mandate the vaccine but medical facilities mandated it for students to be able to perform clinical rotations required for Dordt’s nursing program. Dordt administration denied the exemption. Perry filed a lawsuit under the Iowa Civil Rights Act but a lower court dismissed the lawsuit, finding Perry could not prove he held the religious conviction he cited. The Iowa Supreme Court agreed, finding Perry’s parents held firm beliefs against the COVID-19 vaccine but Perry did not. Among other things, the ruling cited an email from Perry in May 2021 stating “I personally do not have a problem with the vaccine” but that his parents’ beliefs are “the main issue”. The Courts found Perry’s parents had threatened to stop financially supporting him through college if he got the COVID-19 vaccine. The Iowa Supreme Court ruling noted that courts are not allowed to determine whether a specific religious belief is theologically correct or valid, only whether a person truly holds that belief. “Courts may not question the validity of religious principles,” Justice David May wrote in the unanimous opinion. “We cannot say what people should or should not believe. But courts may—and sometimes must—decide what someone actually believes.” Editor’s note: this article has been updated to reflect that Dordt University did not require a COVID-19 vaccine but the medical facilities it partnered with required it for students performing required clinical rotations. content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, October 21, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Three African natural products disrupt SARS-CoV-2 entry and replication in vitro by October 21, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Three African natural products disrupt SARS-CoV-2 entry and replication in vitro Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Three compounds from the pan-African Natural Products Library—oleanolic acid, poinsettifolin B, and rhuschalcone III—disrupted interactions between the SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain and the human ACE2 receptor in laboratory screening. The study identified the molecules as potential antiviral leads for COVID-19, but the findings remain preclinical: the compounds were tested in biochemical and cell-based systems, not in people. Oleanolic acid and rhuschalcone III also reduced SARS-CoV-2 replication in Vero cells at low micromolar concentrations without detectable cytotoxicity under the reported conditions, whereas poinsettifolin B did not show the same antiviral activity in that assay. Researchers screened physical, pure compounds obtained from African medicinal plants in the pan-African Natural Products Library, abbreviated p-ANAPL. The target was the in vitro interaction between the receptor-binding domain, or RBD, of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and ACE2, the host receptor that helps mediate viral entry into cells. Disrupting this molecular interaction could potentially prevent a key step in infection. The library screen selected three compounds with half-maximal inhibitory concentrations, or IC50 values, ranging from 0.5 to 2.4 micromolar, indicating activity within the low-micromolar range in the tested assay. The compounds showed some selectivity in the screening system. Unlike their effects on the SARS-CoV-2 RBD–ACE2 interaction, oleanolic acid, poinsettifolin B, and rhuschalcone III did not disrupt binding between PD-1 and PD-L1, an unrelated host ligand–receptor pair used as a comparator. This result suggests that the observed inhibitory activity was not simply a nonspecific consequence of broadly interfering with protein interactions. The experiment nevertheless measured binding-related activity in vitro, and the authors did not establish that the same effects would occur in an infected organism or lead directly to an effective COVID-19 treatment. Discover more Track Biotech Try Herbs Find Lung Care Monitor Vitals Cell experiments produced a more limited pattern of antiviral activity. Oleanolic acid and rhuschalcone III inhibited SARS-CoV-2 replication in Vero cells at low micromolar concentrations without cytotoxicity at the tested levels. Poinsettifolin B inhibited the RBD–ACE2 interaction but did not inhibit viral replication in this cell model. The distinction is important because interference with receptor binding alone did not guarantee a measurable reduction in viral replication. The evidence also remains specific to the laboratory conditions and cell line used; the study does not show whether the compounds can be safely or effectively administered to humans. Computational modelling provided a possible structural explanation for the three molecules’ activity. The models indicated that each compound could interact with numerous residues on the SARS-CoV-2 RBD and human ACE2, including a subset of sites conserved across SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern. Such models can generate hypotheses about binding modes and guide further experiments, but they do not by themselves confirm a physical interaction in cells or in patients. Overall, the research identifies oleanolic acid, poinsettifolin B, and rhuschalcone III as selective, in vitro antiviral candidates that warrant additional investigation, particularly for settings where access to existing vaccines or therapies is limited. It is also expected to be effective for Omicron. 29 Des 2021 09:22 WIB · English Kecil Sedang Besar Sangat Besar Bagikan Salin Pranala Temukan Kami di Google Oleh IQBAL MOCHTAR Facing Omicron with Vigilance without Panic English 00:00 00:00 10 10 1.00x Didie SW The Omicron variant has entered Indonesia. According to Health Ministry data as of Saturday (25/12/2021), based on whole genome sequencing results, the number of cases in Indonesia has reached 46. A month after being identified in South Africa, 77 countries have reported the presence of this variant. Its entry into Indonesia had in fact been predicted. Some experts even believe there were many cases of this variant even before its detection. The World Health Organization (WHO) also had the same view. This variant had presumably spread over many countries although it was not yet detected or reported. Omicron is the 15th variant. Like the previous variants, at least four aspects related to Omicron arouse the concern of experts: its high transmissibility, its clinical effect and severity, its potential for reinfection and its effect on vaccine efficacy. The capacity and speed of transmission is the new variant’s crucial issue. Several reports have concluded that the Omicron variant spreads sporadically and rapidly. Its transmission is considered phenomenal as it far exceeds the spread of preceding variants, including the Delta variant. The French Prime Minister even described it as spreading at lightning speed. The number of people infected has been recorded as doubling within just 2-3 days. Also read: > Omicron and Global Management of the Pandemic > Health Ethics during the Pandemic Just compare it with Delta’s doubling rate of 10-12 days. As a result of its transmission speed, Omicron has promptly dominated the Covid-19 variant map. In the United States, only within a week the proportion of Omicron rose sevenfold from 0.4 to 2.9 percent. In Britain, its proportion increased from 20 to 44 percent in several days. The European Center for Diseases and Prevention Control has estimated that in January this variant will dominate Covid-19 in the entire European continent. Iklan Iklan There are many hypotheses of this transmission rate. In the respiratory tract, this variant can multiply very rapidly, dozens of times faster than does the Delta variant. Its amount can also shoot up in the tissue only within 48 hours after infection. The high transmissibility becomes a specter for the health service system. The escape of one or several cases into a country can trigger sporadic transmission. Within a short time, many people can be infected and seek health service. Some of them certainly need hospital treatment, oxygen and drugs. The rapid and sporadic spread has the potential to lead to an overload that threatens the stability of health service. The collapse of health service is imminent. Kompas As for its clinical effect and the severity caused, there are conflicting hypotheses. Doctors in South Africa have reported that patients’ complaints and clinical symptoms are mostly mild in nature. Most of them have a slight cough, runny nose and get exhausted. Only a few need hospital treatment and none of them have died. Although the Omicron variant has dominated the Covid-19 transmission map in South Africa, there are no signs of increasing necessity for hospital service. Even compared with the time when the Delta variant was dominant, the need for hospital treatment at present is 30 percent lower. In Johannesburg, 90 percent of Covid-19 cases are dominated by the Omicron variant but the rate of hospital treatment has not risen. This serves as the reason for some experts’ argument that there is no indication of Omicron causing severity of illness or fatality. However, the WHO views it from the other side. It is premature to conclude that this variant does not cause illness severity. The reason is that this variant is new and the cases observed are limited in number. The theory and model of disease transmission suggest that the fatal effect of a new variant can be noticed if the number of cases observed is quite large and the duration is longer. It means that the current number of cases is not adequate to draw any conclusion. Also read: > Third Wave of Pandemic, Threat or Illusion? > Superspreading Events and Vaccination Coverage Iklan Iklan In realty, every day a lot more information appears about this variant. Recently, a confirmed case of this variant in Britain was reported to have died. The variant’s capacity to cause reinfection in people already developing antibodies also gives reason for serious concern. Theoretically and empirically, people who have been infected or vaccinated build up antibodies that protect them from Covid-19 for a certain period. Omicron disturbs this protection and has the potential to cause reinfection. In South Africa, most of its population has once been infected with Covid-19 and developed antibodies. When Omicron emerged, many of these people were reinfected. This means that the antibodies induced by their previous infections do not provide protection against Omicron. Research in the US also has the same result, in which 80 percent of those infected with Omicron turn out to have received two vaccine doses and even almost half of them have got booster shots. Nearly one fifth of patients also have suffered from Covid-19, meaning that the antibodies derived from previous infections or vaccinations prove to give no protection against Omicron. Kompas Regarding its effect on vaccines, several days ago Pfizer announced its initial study results, which are quite worrisome. The protective effect of the Pfizer vaccine declines significantly in the face of the Omicron variant. In people already receiving two vaccine doses and being infected with Omicron, their amounts of antibodies decrease 25-fold compared with those infected with the original virus. The efficacy of the vaccine is reduced to 0-20 percent. When booster doses are injected, the amounts of antibodies can again increase, raising the efficacy to 55-80 percent. This means that two vaccine doses do not effectively protect against this variant. Therefore, booster shots are needed. The vaccine efficacy decline involves not only the Pfizer vaccine, but also those of Moderna and AstraZeneca. Some experts make the extrapolation that other vaccines will also undergo efficacy decrease when they encounter the Omicron variant. The declining vaccine efficacy against Omicron has been predicted. The reason is that Omicron has more than 50 mutations, 30 of which involved the spike protein that becomes the target of various vaccines. As the target is mutating and changing, vaccines cannot work effectively. They miss the target. Also read: > Omicron Variant Transmission Expanding Iklan Iklan > World Races Against Omicron Variant To overcome it, booster doses or vaccine modifications are needed. This of course creates a new problem. Let alone booster shots, many countries are even faltering in their attempts to broaden the coverage of first and second dose vaccinations. In South Africa, the people already receiving first doses only constitute 31 percent and second doses 26 percent. In Indonesia, the first-dose coverage of its population is 55 percent and second-dose 36 percent. Globally, over 40 countries have not yet vaccinated 10 percent of their populations. Under such limitations, how can the countries prepare booster injections to face the Omicron variant? Sporadic but mild? Mutations and variants are the natural process of viruses. This phenomenon will keep going as long as viruses continue to exist. The Omicron variant is the 15th metamorphosis continuum of Covid-19. As long as the pandemic is not yet effectively handled, new variants will keep arising. Some variants may be less lethal and not dangerous but others can be the reverse. To date, the Delta variant is still considered the most dangerous one. Its magnitude of morbidity and mortality is indeed serious. Yet the appearance of Omicron can change the variant distribution map. Some experts believe that before long the Omicron variant will take over the Delta variant’s domination all over the world. Kompas Although Omicron studies are still ongoing, experts have different views of the magnitude of this variant. First, some are convinced that this variant will have a serious negative impact on the development of the pandemic. It causes the rates of infection, sickness, severity and mortality to rise significantly. Consequently, the pandemic is expected to last longer. The yo-yo phenomenon will continue to occur. The acceleration- deceleration-plateau graphs of cases and deaths will keep going on. Countries will repeatedly impose lockdowns and allow relaxation. The pandemic control is trapped in a vicious cycle. The world economy will remain gloomy. Second, other experts adopt a more optimistic stance. Although the faster and sporadic transmission of Omicron has been confirmed, they expect a milder clinical effect and illness severity. In other words, there’s no problem with the rapid spread as long as it’s not severe. Sporadic and fast but mild. Indeed, so far there has been no solid evidence yet that this virus produces a high rate of severity and fatality. If later the assumption of being sporadic and fast but mild is correct, this condition is just seen as a blessing in disguise. A loss that brings goodness. With its high transmission rate, this variant will replace the Delta variant’s domination. Owing to its mild effect, the serious morbidity and mortality of the Delta variant will be replaced by the morbidity and mortality of less lethal Omicron. It means that Omicron is at large but not dangerous. With its high transmission rate, this variant will replace the Delta variant’s domination. Today it is premature to determine which assumption in more accurate. The journey of Omicron has only lasted for over a month. Many things about this variant are still obscure. Experts keep focusing on and examining the various sides of this variant. This is crucial especially to anticipate the worst that may arise from it. The WHO has warned the world against feeling panic in the face of new variants, including Omicron, let alone implementing super-tight steps without being founded on clear clinical and epidemiologic evidence. Over-restrictive policies will just result in inefficient management. While furthering its studies, the WHO has warned the world to keep vigilance. The world is encountering a new virus whose structure can change at any moment. As a result, its morbidity and mortality may also change. Interestingly, despite the changing structure, morbidity and mortality of the virus, it can be managed in the same way by implementing 3M (mask wearing, hand washing, distancing) + 3T (testing, tracing, treatment) + vaccination. The 3M + 3T + vaccination management has proved to be effective for the original Covid-19 strain and other variants. It is also expected to be effective for Omicron. So, some experts have every reason to say, “Whatever the variant may be, it should be managed by 3M + 3T + vaccination”. content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, October 22, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Case report: uncertain crying episodes during infant SARS-CoV-2 infection by October 22, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Case report: uncertain crying episodes during infant SARS-CoV-2 infection Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A 44-day-old term female infant with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection experienced two crying-triggered episodes of marked pallor, limpness and reduced responsiveness after crying had ceased, according to a case report in Frontiers in Pediatrics . Both episodes ended with spontaneous recovery, but the cause could not be definitively established because neither event was recorded with physiological monitoring. The infant experienced no further episodes during hospitalization or throughout eight weeks of follow-up, the report said. This absence of recurrence was an observed outcome rather than proof of the underlying mechanism. Because the case involved one patient, it cannot establish how frequently such events occur during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection or whether the infection contributed to the episodes. The reported sequence suggested breath-holding spells as one possible explanation. That possibility was based on the timing of the episodes: crying was followed by pallor, reduced muscle tone and diminished responsiveness, and the infant recovered spontaneously. The report also considered infection-associated apnea and other causes of paroxysmal events in early infancy, leaving several explanations in the differential diagnosis. The source report does not provide such contemporaneous recordings for either event. Discover more Book Care Services Check Symptoms Study Biology infection Shop Baby Gear As a result, the investigators could not confirm a specific physiological disturbance or determine which mechanism produced the pallor, hypotonia and reduced responsiveness. That uncertainty is central to the case. The report therefore describes the infant’s episodes as a diagnostic dilemma rather than assigning a confirmed diagnosis. The authors emphasize careful differential diagnosis for crying-triggered pallid and hypotonic episodes occurring during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. The case instead documents a temporal association between an acute infection and two unexplained episodes in one infant. The report was published in the General Pediatrics and Pediatric Emergency Care section of Frontiers in Pediatrics . It is a case report, not a controlled study or population-level analysis, and the authors identify diagnostic uncertainty as the main feature of the case. No physiological data were captured during the two events, limiting the ability to distinguish among the potential explanations. For science reporting, the most defensible conclusion is narrow: an infant with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection had two episodes of pallor, hypotonia and reduced responsiveness after crying stopped, recovered spontaneously from each event, and had no reported recurrence during hospitalization or eight weeks of follow-up. The clinical sequence was compatible with breath-holding spells, but infection-associated apnea and other paroxysmal causes remained possible. The case illustrates the importance of preserving diagnostic uncertainty when the events themselves are not physiologically documented. Mechanisms of Action of Auranofin and Remdesivir 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年10月24日 来源:Advanced Science 14.1 编辑推荐: 金诺芬(Auranofin)为FDA批准的口服抗风湿药物,研究人员既往证实其在临床前模型中可抑制严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2型(SARS-CoV-2)复制与病理进程。本研究通过生化药物-蛋白互作、细胞机制实验及临床前药效研究系统阐释其作用机制(MOA):金诺芬 欢迎领取《全方位集成的高通量阵列式 SPR 平台》 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 RESEARCH ARTICLE Open Access 金诺芬(Auranofin)为FDA批准的口服抗风湿药物,研究人员既往证实其在临床前模型中可抑制严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2型(SARS-CoV-2)复制与病理进程。本研究通过生化药物-蛋白互作、细胞机制实验及临床前药效研究系统阐释其作用机制(MOA):金诺芬直接结合并抑制SARS-CoV-2主蛋白酶(MPro,亦称3CLpro),同时靶向病毒生命周期多阶段,扰乱内体运输、抑制刺突(Spike)S1/S2蛋白酶解加工、削弱合胞体(syncytia)形成,并衰减NF-κB驱动的促炎信号。在细胞培养中,金诺芬与瑞德西韦(Remdesivir)呈强协同,但与MPro抑制剂奈玛特韦(Nirmatrelvir)竞争结合。感染SARS-CoV-2德尔塔(Delta)变异株小鼠中,金诺芬与瑞德西韦前药GS-621763的口服联用优于单药,显著降低病毒复制、炎性细胞因子反应与肺病理,改善临床结局。上述发现确立金诺芬多靶点抗病毒MOA,并为抗COVID-19全口服联合方案提供机制依据。 研究背景与立项依据 欢迎领取《CGT 研发全流程解决方案》领 取 《Advanced Science》刊发的这项研究聚焦严重COVID-19治疗困境。SARS-CoV-2持续进化流行,直接作用抗病毒药(DAA)易遇耐药突变,宿主导向抗病毒药(HDA)可调控病理炎症但单药有限。金诺芬系含铜(原文为金)FDA获批抗风湿制剂,前期提示抗SARS-CoV-2活性,但直接病毒靶点互作不清。研究人员据此系统解析其机制,并设计全口服联合方案以提升疗效、降低炎症损伤。 主要技术方法 研究采用生化与细胞学关键手段:等温滴定量热(ITC)与计算对接验证药物-蛋白结合;荧光报告系统包括FlipGFP-Mpro探针评估MPro活性、双荧光素酶报告量化RNA依赖RNA聚合酶(RdRp)与NF-κB转录;split-GFP互补法检测合胞体;共聚焦显微观测内体运输与ACE2分布;流式与Western blot分析刺突加工。动物端以K18-hACE2转基因小鼠(Jackson Laboratory品系)经鼻感染临床分离Delta株,开展药代与防治给药,结合qRT-PCR、斑块 assay及细胞因子谱评价。 研究结果 2.1 金诺芬损害SARS-CoV-2入胞与内体运输:借假病毒与时效加法实验,发现药物不阻受体结合,但扰乱ACE2膜定位、降低病毒颗粒早期内体(EEA1阳性)共定位,抑制内吞后运输。 2.2 金诺芬抑制Mpro而非RdRp:FlipGFP-Mpro报告示GFP信号降约40%;时序给药与复制子双荧光素酶证明不改变病毒RNA、核衣壳蛋白(NP)及RdRp功能,机制独立于复制期抑制。 2.3 金诺芬直接结合Mpro并与奈玛特韦竞争:ITC得野生型KD=197±16.6 μM,催化突变C145A亲和力大降;顺序滴定显示两药占位重叠,联用奈玛特韦无益。 2.4 抑制刺突加工与合胞体:split-GFP见融合减约50%;Western blot示S2/S0比下降,S2′(K814R突变验证)加工受抑,解释入胞与细胞间传播受阻。 2.5 衰减NF-κB信号:TNF-α刺激下转录抑约30%,感染中抑超3倍,伴TNF-α、IL-6下调,抗炎贡献明确。 2.6 与核苷类似物协同:ZIP模型示金诺芬-瑞德西韦ZIP=10.19强协同;与莫努匹韦弱协同,与奈玛特韦负协同。GS-621763体外对香港株、Delta、Omicron均压低病毒载量。 2.7 体内联用增效:单剂口服药代示GS-441524速达峰、金示踪金(Au)持续。K18-hACE2小鼠中,预防/治疗联用改善临床评分、体重维持与生存,肺vRNA再降,IL-6/TNF-α削减,且半量GS-621763加金诺芬达等效,呈现剂量节省。 讨论与结论翻译 讨论指出,金诺芬经金属(金)配位多靶点作用:入胞干扰、Mpro直接抑制、刺突加工阻断、NF-κB消炎,互补RdRp抑制剂。联用提升屏障抗耐药潜力,局限含HEK293-ACE2缺TMPRSS2主要反映组织蛋白酶途径,短期高剂量人体毒理待补。 研究结论:金诺芬抑制SARS-CoV-2 Mpro为其主要抗病毒机制,刺突加工与入胞为附加活动,免疫调节提供宿主导向获益;二者互补致与GS-621763强协同,实现增强抗病毒、剂量节省与炎症缓解。该临床前证据支持机制驱动的全口服金诺芬-瑞德西韦组合策略,亦为冠状病毒感染宿主导向治疗提供普适思路。 这篇论文解读已完成,接下来可以选择一个方向继续深化: 把全文解读改写成期刊审稿意见 梳理机制证据链并标出薄弱节点 把全文解读改写成期刊审稿意见 content: Search analysis, research, academics... Arts + Culture Economy Education Environment + Energy Ethics + Religion Health Politics + Society Science + Tech World Podcasts Local Conservative member of Parliament Dean Allison, left, and lawyer Shawn Buckley hold a press conference on Parliament Hill in Ottawa on June 4, 2026, to announce an inquiry into Canadian COVID-19 vaccine-injured persons. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Sean Kilpatrick An inquiry into alleged COVID‐19 vaccine injuries fails to weigh the ethics and risks of Canada’s response Published: October 21, 2026 8:18am EDT In early September, Conservative Party MP Dean Allison held a four-day independent, unsanctioned “inquiry” for “Canadians to share their personal experiences of injuries...from the COVID-19 vaccine(s).” The event heard testimony that alleged the response to COVID-19 was “a miserable failure,” not least due to the “assaults on freedom and other malign actions.” An opinion piece in the Toronto Sun subsequently claimed that COVID-19 vaccine programs “killed thousands of Canadians,” repeating a call for an immediate stop of COVID-19 mRNA vaccinations, as well as “resignations, arrests and a full public inquiry...by the prime minister.” It further claimed that Canada’s COVID-19 vaccination efforts represent, at best, the “biggest health policy mistake in Canadian history.” But testimony heard at this inquiry — and responses to that testimony — conflate factual claims with ethical claims. As a consequence, it fails to recognize the ethical factors critical to understanding and justifying COVID-19 vaccination efforts. As public health ethicists, we’re interested in clarifying the factors necessary to substantiate claims about “policy mistakes” and informing expectations for future vaccination policy decisions. The conflation of facts and ethics Some of the claims made in the Allison inquiry and related reporting pertained to facts, both stated and omitted. Other claims were ethical in nature. The difference is critical to understanding and justifying COVID-19 vaccination efforts. For example, questions of facts are: How many people were injured or died as a result of COVID-19 vaccination How were vaccine candidates tested and regulated How many people were saved by vaccines. Immunity & Society, a new series from The Conversation Canada in partnership with the Bridge Research Consortium. Immunity and Society is a new series from The Conversation Canada that presents new vaccine discoveries and immune-based innovations that are changing how we understand and protect human health. Through a partnership with the Bridge Research Consortium, these articles — written by experts in Canada at the forefront of immunology, biomanufacturing, social science and humanities — explore the latest developments and their impacts. Getting on the same page about these facts and dispelling mis- and disinformation remains crucial. For example, the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) records 455 reports of deaths following COVID-19 vaccination, noting these deaths weren’t necessarily attributable to the vaccine. After assessing causality, PHAC reports a total of four deaths consistent with causal association to immunization. To put this in context, more than 100 million COVID-19 vaccine doses have been administered in Canada. But getting on the same page about facts is not enough. That’s because claims about whether the government is justified in imposing certain obligations or burdens on the public — for example, requirements that citizens get vaccinated — are not answerable by facts alone. These are questions of ethics. These claims are about what one should do or what governments have legitimate authority to do, morally speaking: in other words, what is considered good or right or just. Values and policy decisions Such ethical claims are a matter of values, which people or groups may prioritize differently. For example, in deciding on health policy options, some may prefer the option that preserves personal autonomy above all else. Others may prioritize fairness and the policy option that minimizes deaths or health disparities. And some may locate the preservation of autonomy in policy options that are fair for all and that saves lives. Critically, no policy decision is ever free of values and value judgments. All policy decisions, including those related to vaccination, involve trade-offs of competing values. That necessarily means there will be trade-offs in the distribution of benefits, risks and burdens experienced across individuals and groups in society. While evidence can tell us what those benefits, risks and burdens might be, it cannot by itself tell us what the right trade-off is. That is, whether it is ethically justifiable to limit autonomy in some ways in order to preserve autonomy in others or to protect certain segments of the population from severe illness or death. In other words, facts alone will not determine how those competing values should be balanced, what outcomes matter the most and whose interests should be prioritized, among other things. Discussions about the legitimacy of Canada’s COVID-19 vaccination efforts or determining whether it was the “biggest health policy mistake in Canadian history” requires not only solid scientific facts, but also explicit ethical reasoning. This entails careful analysis of the values at stake, how trade-offs may reasonably be made between those values and ultimately what governments are ethically justified in doing in the name of public health. Syringes and vials of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine are seen on a work surface during a drive-through clinic at St. Lawrence College in Kingston, Ont. in December 2021. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Lars Hagberg The ethics of imposing risk Fundamentally, the nature of the ethical claims made throughout the Allison inquiry and relevant reporting relate to one’s freedom to choose whether to be placed at risk by taking the COVID-19 vaccine. Yet, as our research argues, such claims about vaccine risks often fail to acknowledge or attend to the reciprocal nature of those risks and the reciprocal nature of freedom. At the same time that we may be exposed to risk when getting vaccinated (since no medical intervention is entirely risk-free), we also impose risk on others by choosing to forgo vaccination or choosing policy options that fail to effectively address vaccine-preventable diseases. Just as having the freedom to engage in an activity necessarily entails accepting some of the risks that are created in doing that activity, imposing risks on others can correspondingly justify limits being placed on one’s freedoms. A useful example is driving a car: Choosing to drive means accepting risks to one’s own safety, and it also imposes risks on other road users. Those risks to others can justify restricting the freedom to drive at high speeds by imposing and enforcing speed limits. The existence of risk alone doesn’t preclude governments from implementing policy or health interventions. Every choice carries risk, including the choice not to act. While vaccines themselves do entail some small risks, they are used to reduce a much greater risk of disease that people may not be able to avoid or mitigate on their own. Vaccination policies are not implemented against a backdrop of zero risk, and so doing nothing — such as choosing not to introduce vaccination policies — also creates risk. In certain situations, such as pandemics, it can create more risk, and governments should be accountable for these risks as well. Some of the statements made at the Allison inquiry and in corresponding media coverage appear to hold that governments cannot impose risk on the public. From an ethical standpoint, this is not a given, especially when action and inaction both involve risk. Such claims need further ethical analysis and reasoning that examines the nature of the risks and benefits, how they are distributed and the strength of the justifications used to defend policy action or inaction. Greater attention to ethics in policymaking and evaluation is critical to help identify the values at the heart of policy prescriptions, including related to freedom and risk, and to separate factual uncertainty from disagreement about those values. Only then will we be able to have constructive discussion about vaccination and vaccine policy in Canada. ideation spiked significantly among older U.S. adults after COVID-19 pandemic Researchers say many affected adults did not have traditional risk factors, highlighting potential gaps in prevention frameworks Credit: iStockPhoto October 23, 2026 By Will Houston 3 min read New research from UCLA Health and UC San Diego Health found a significant spike in suicidal thoughts, planning and attempts among older U.S. adults in the years following the COVID-19 pandemic. The study, published in the Journal of Affective Disorders, used data from nearly 42,500 adults aged 50 or older surveyed during the National Survey on Drug Use and Health from 2021 to 2024. The analysis found: Suicidal ideation increased 42.6%, suicide planning by 256.2% and suicide attempts by 263.3% Increases in suicidal ideation and planning were concentrated among individuals without traditional risk factors such as major depression or alcohol use, raising questions about whether current screening frameworks are missing a growing at-risk population Suicide planning increased significantly more steeply among those with past-year cannabis use compared to those without (449.9% vs. 188.3% increase) “These findings suggest that many older adults who are struggling are not the ones our current screening approaches are designed to catch,” said the study’s lead author Dr. Kevin Yang, a psychiatrist, research fellow at the UCLA National Clinician Scholars Program and graduate student at the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health. “If a growing share of suicidal thoughts and plans is showing up in people without a depression diagnosis or recent substance use, we need to rethink how we identify risk and reach older adults before a crisis occurs.” Suicide prevention for older adults relies heavily on screening for depression and other mental health conditions. The authors state that the findings point to a need for broader risk assessment that could include factors such as social isolation, loneliness, bereavement, financial strain and frailty, in addition to other established risk factors such as depression. Yang said continued monitoring of emerging at-risk groups is needed. Further research is also warranted on what leads older adults from suicidal thoughts to planning and on how cannabis use affects mental health over time. The authors note that the study was exploratory and its findings should be interpreted cautiously. The survey captures a snapshot in time, so it cannot show why the increases occurred or establish cause and effect. Responses were self-reported; the survey excludes people living in institutions such as hospitals. Additionally, the total number of reported suicide attempts was relatively small (n=113). The authors also note that the results likely underestimate the full burden of suicidal behavior, because the survey cannot capture people who died by suicide. The study was supported by the National Institute on Drug Abuse and the Sam and Rose Stein Institute for Research on Aging at UC San Diego. The study was conducted while Yang was a resident psychiatrist at UC San Diego Health. If you are in crisis, emotional distress or concerned about someone, call, text, or chat 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline for free, confidential support from a trained counselor, available 24/7. content_title: Why did people report feeling better during COVID-19? A French study offers clues
content: Despite the upheaval of COVID-19, French participants reported higher well-being scores during the pandemic, while researchers found that everyday illness symptoms had a far greater association with how people felt than seasonal or demographic factors. Study: Evolution and determinants of subjective well-being in the French general population between 2014 and 2023. Image credit: sommart sombutwanitkul/Shutterstock.com A recent BMC Public Health study assessed longitudinal trends in subjective well-being and identified key associated factors, including health status, sociodemographic variables, acute symptom burden, seasonality, and the COVID-19 pandemic period, in a French participatory surveillance cohort from 2014 to 2023. Evolution and current gaps in subjective well-being research Much more than physical health shapes how people feel about their lives. Subjective well-being (SWB), which encompasses emotions, life satisfaction, and a sense of purpose, is influenced by social, economic, and environmental conditions. Researchers increasingly view it as an important indicator of individual well-being and broader societal health. Once largely a topic of philosophical debate, well-being has become a major focus of scientific research and public policy. Since the mid-20th century, advances in measurement have helped researchers explore how happiness and life satisfaction relate to health, finances, and social circumstances. More recently, growing recognition that economic growth alone cannot capture quality of life has placed well-being at the center of wider discussions about public health and sustainability. Yet important questions remain about how well-being changes when people become ill. Although the relationship between general health and well-being is well established, less is known about the effects of short-term infectious illnesses, particularly during seasonal outbreaks. Researchers also face the challenge of separating the effects of winter itself from those of the increased illness burden that typically accompanies it. The COVID-19 pandemic has added another layer of uncertainty. While numerous studies have examined its immediate effects on well-being, fewer have tracked how people's perceptions of their health and well-being changed over longer periods, including before, during, and after the pandemic emergency. Assessing subjective well-being in the French population between 2014 and 2023 The current study used data from Grippenet/Covidnet, a French online influenza surveillance system within the European Influenzanet platform. Participants registered voluntarily and anonymously and completed a baseline survey on sociodemographic characteristics, medical history, and lifestyle habits. Each influenza season (November–May), participants received weekly reminders to self-report health status and symptoms and rate their overall well-being in response to the question, “Overall, how are you feeling?” on a 0–100 scale. This single-item measure primarily captured perceived health-related well-being. Symptomatic individuals reported new symptoms unrelated to chronic conditions. Reporting was flexible, and participants could submit data at any frequency. The study spanned nine winter seasons (2014–2015 to 2022–2023) and included adults (≥18 years) residing in mainland France who completed at least one intake and one weekly survey per season. Sociodemographic variables included gender, age group, education (≤high school, >high school), household composition, occupational status, residence (urban/rural), transport, smoking status, contact patterns, chronic medication, and the French Deprivation Index. Weekly surveys recorded symptom count (0, 1–2, 3–5, >5), but symptom cause was excluded from the adjusted analysis. Seasons were grouped as pre-pandemic (2014–2015 to week 10, 2019–2020), pandemic (week 11, 2019–2020 to 2021–2022), and post-emergency (2022–2023). Participants missing age, gender, or education data were excluded. Participants' demographics and trends in influenza-like illness and COVID-19 Over nine seasons, 16,065 individuals contributed a total of 54,861 registrations. Participation peaked in 2019–2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, when 10,448 participants were active, then gradually declined in subsequent years. Demographic weighting aligned the sample with the 2022 French population in age, gender, and education, but these variables reflect statistical adjustments rather than real shifts in the cohort and should not be compared across seasons. Most participants, 78% to 81% depending on the year, lived in urban areas. The proportion reporting regular medication for a chronic condition ranged from 26% to 41% across seasons. Weekly symptom surveys showed that 78–92% of responses reported no symptoms. Reports of 1–2 symptoms ranged from 5–12%, 3–5 symptoms from 2–7%, and more than 5 symptoms from 1–4%. Most symptoms were attributed to "other causes" (57–74%). Reports of influenza-like illness (ILI) declined from 17% of symptomatic questionnaires in 2014–2015 to 2% in 2020–2021, before rising to 12% in 2022–2023. COVID-19 was cited as the cause in 8% (2019–2020), 6% (2020–2021), 23% (2021–2022), and 9% (2022–2023) of symptomatic surveys. Seasonal variation and subjective well-being trends and influences Self-reported well-being rose over the study period, with median scores increasing from 86 in 2014–2015 to 93 in 2020–2021. Health status appeared to play a major role in how participants felt. Those reporting no symptoms consistently had higher well-being scores, with medians ranging from 90 to 94, compared with 59 to 75 among those experiencing symptoms. Among participants with laboratory-confirmed infections, those with influenza reported particularly low well-being scores, with medians of 44–48, compared with 50–60 among those with COVID-19. However, the difference was statistically significant only in 2021–2022. The researchers cautioned that the small number of confirmed influenza cases and differences in testing practices limited these comparisons. Looking at trends over time, well-being scores remained relatively stable from 2014–2015 through 2019–2020 before rising sharply in 2020–2021. Scores remained elevated in 2021–2022, although the increase was less pronounced. A recurring winter dip was also observed between mid-December and mid-March, largely reflecting the greater number of participants reporting illness symptoms during these months. The researchers also identified several demographic and lifestyle factors associated with well-being. Higher scores were linked to being male, aged 65 or older, living with others, having higher education, and having contact with patients. Students, retirees, unemployed individuals, and those on sick leave or staying at home also reported higher scores after adjustment for other factors. However, the researchers cautioned that some of these unexpected occupational associations could reflect selection effects or other unmeasured differences rather than benefits associated with those circumstances. Well-being was also higher during the pandemic and post-emergency periods. After accounting for other factors, scores averaged approximately two points higher on the 0–100 scale in both periods compared with before the pandemic. In contrast, contact with children, smoking, regular medication for chronic conditions, and winter were associated with lower scores. Of all the factors examined, symptom burden showed by far the strongest negative association with well-being. Compared with participants reporting no symptoms, those with one or two symptoms scored approximately 15 points lower, those with three to five symptoms scored 26 points lower, and those with more than five symptoms scored 40 points lower after adjustment. The French Deprivation Index showed mixed associations with well-being, without a consistent pattern across deprivation levels. Meanwhile, no statistically significant associations were observed for middle-aged adults, urban residents, public transport users, or participants reporting contact with older people or groups of at least 10 individuals. Conclusion This study analyzed subjective well-being in a French participatory surveillance cohort from 2014 to 2023. Acute symptom burden, particularly during winter, was strongly associated with most short-term declines in self-rated well-being. An increase in well-being scores during the COVID-19 pandemic may reflect reduced respiratory virus circulation, selective participation, or other unmeasured factors, though these could not be directly assessed. Sociodemographic differences, including a persistent gender gap, shaped baseline well-being. However, the voluntary online cohort was not fully representative of the French population, and demographic weighting could not eliminate selection bias. The observational design, reliance on a single-item measure that predominantly reflected perceived health-related well-being, and lack of detailed psychological and social data also limit causal interpretation and generalizability. These results highlight the promise and challenges of participatory surveillance for monitoring population well-being and emphasize the importance of addressing measurement and selection biases in future research. - Guets, A.J. et al. (2026). Evolution and determinants of subjective well-being in the French general population between 2014 and 2023. BMC Public Health. 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Article | Open Access 多种针对不同呼吸道病原体的疫苗联合接种可能有助于提高接种覆盖率并简化成人免疫程序。研究人员在中国开展了一项随机、多中心、开放标签的IV期临床试验(注册于中国临床试验注册中心,编号ChiCTR2100046227),旨在评估将灭活SARS-CoV-2疫苗(WIBP-CorV)与23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗(PPV23)及四价灭活流感疫苗(IIV4)联合接种的免疫原性和安全性。共计1404名年龄≥18岁的成人入组,其中18–59岁和≥60岁年龄段人数相等,按1:1:1的比例随机分配至三组:第0天接种WIBP-CorV+PPV23、第28天接种WIBP-CorV+IIV4组;单独在第0天和第28天接种WIBP-CorV组;或第0天接种PPV23、第28天接种IIV4组。联合接种在各疫苗平台间均保持了体液免疫应答。对于SARS-CoV-2中和抗体及肺炎球菌血清型特异性IgG应答,几何平均滴度或浓度的非劣效性得以证实。所有肺炎球菌血清型的血清转换率均不劣于单独接种,但SARS-CoV-2(第二剂后)和甲型流感(H1N1)的结果一致性较差。按年龄分层的分析显示了与年龄和毒株相关的非劣效性结果,这些结果应谨慎解读。联合接种的安全性可接受,仅轻度、一过性局部反应发生率略有升高,未发生与疫苗相关的严重不良事件(SAEs)。这些发现支持在本研究纳入的成人人群中,将WIBP-CorV与PPV23和IIV4联合接种在维持免疫原性和安全性方面具有可行性。 研究背景与目的 下载安捷伦药物开发中的线粒体毒性评估《案例研究》领 取 呼吸道传染病,包括新型冠状病毒病(COVID-19)、季节性流感和肺炎球菌感染,在全球范围内持续造成巨大负担。截至2023年3月,全球报告超过7.6亿例COVID-19病例和680万例相关死亡。流感病毒每年导致多达500万例重症季节性流感和29万至65万例流感相关呼吸道死亡。肺炎球菌疾病则是肺炎和脓毒症的主要原因,每年约导致100万儿童死亡,并在老年人中造成显著的肺炎死亡率。这三种感染位列全球传染病致死的主要原因之一。 疫苗接种是预防这些疾病最有效且最具成本效益的策略。世界卫生组织(WHO)和许多国家现在提倡联合接种疫苗,即在同一次就诊中给予所有需要的疫苗,以提高便利性、免疫效率和社区保护。然而,关于将COVID-19疫苗与流感疫苗和肺炎球菌疫苗同时接种的综合证据仍然有限。此前的研究规模较小或人群特异,缺乏来自大规模随机试验的全面证据。 为此,研究人员在中国开展了一项大型、随机、多中心、开放标签、对照、非劣效性IV期临床试验,旨在评估在年龄≥18岁的成人(包括预设的18–59岁和≥60岁年龄组)中,将灭活SARS-CoV-2疫苗(WIBP-CorV)分别与23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗(PPV23)和四价灭活流感疫苗(IIV4)联合接种的免疫原性和安全性。 研究方法 本研究是一项在中国三个省级研究中心(湖北、广东、河南)开展的随机、开放标签、多中心、对照、非劣效性IV期临床试验。共招募了1404名健康成人(年龄≥18岁),并按1:1:1的比例随机分配到三组:联合接种组(第0天接种WIBP-CorV+PPV23,第28天接种WIBP-CorV+IIV4)、单独WIBP-CorV组(第0天和第28天接种WIBP-CorV)、以及PPV23/IIV4单独组(第0天接种PPV23,第28天接种IIV4)。参与者被前瞻性地按年龄分层(18–59岁和≥60岁),并确保两个年龄层人数大致相等。研究采用分层区组随机化方案,按年龄组和研究中心进行分层。这是一项开放标签试验,但实验室人员和统计学家对分组情况不知情。血液样本在第0天(基线)、第28天和第56天采集,用于免疫原性评估。安全性监测持续6个月。主要免疫原性终点包括SARS-CoV-2中和抗体的血清转换率和抗体滴度、23种肺炎球菌血清型特异性IgG浓度、以及四种流感毒株的血凝抑制(HI)抗体滴度。非劣效性界值设定为:几何平均滴度/浓度比值的95%置信区间下限≥0.67,或血清转换率组间差异的95%置信区间下限≥?10%。 研究结果 SARS-CoV-2中和抗体:无论单独接种还是联合接种,WIBP-CorV均诱导了中和抗体应答的显著升高。在总体人群和18–59岁参与者中,第28天和第56天的几何平均滴度(GMTs)在组间相当,几何平均滴度比值(GMRs)满足非劣效性标准。然而,在≥60岁的参与者中,第56天时非劣效性未达到,因为GMR的95%置信区间下限低于0.67。尽管如此,两组的抗体水平相似,几何平均增长倍数无统计学显著差异。 肺炎球菌多糖抗体:对于PPV23,联合接种组在第28天所有23种肺炎球菌血清型的血清转换率范围为62.75%至95.79%,均满足非劣效性标准。在18–59岁成人中,少数血清型的血清转换率略低于PPV23/IIV4单独组,而≥60岁参与者的所有血清型转换率均更高。几何平均浓度比值(GMRs)在总体人群中范围为0.88至1.07,所有95%置信区间下限均≥0.67,表明联合接种未损害IgG应答。 流感抗体:到第56天,联合接种组针对四种流感毒株(A(H1N1)、A(H3N2)、B/Yamagata、B/Victoria)的血清转换率范围为74.28%至90.97%。与PPV23/IIV4单独组相比,联合接种组除A(H1N1)外,其他所有毒株均满足非劣效性标准。年龄分层分析显示,某些亚组中个别毒株的非劣效性勉强未达到。重要的是,基于GMT的免疫原性终点在所有四个毒株中均显示联合接种组与对照组相当,GMRs满足非劣效性标准。18–59岁成人的GMTs普遍较高,而≥60岁老年人的抗体应答分布更窄。 安全性:联合接种组疫苗相关局部不良反应的发生率(31.83%)高于PPV23/IIV4单独组(20.13%),主要由注射部位疼痛驱动。全身性不良反应发生率较低(联合接种组为7.31%),各组间无统计学显著差异。大多数不良反应为轻度(1级),极少出现重度(3级)事件。在6个月的随访期间,共14名参与者发生严重不良事件(SAEs),发生率在各组间无显著差异,且所有SAEs均被评估为与研究疫苗无关。未发生与疫苗相关的SAEs或死亡。 讨论与结论 这项多中心随机IV期试验表明,按照研究接种方案(第0天接种WIBP-CorV+PPV23,第28天接种WIBP-CorV+IIV4)进行联合接种,能够产生与单独接种相当的免疫应答,并保持可接受的安全性。尽管在某些亚组(特别是老年人中的A(H1N1)和B/Yamagata)中,血清转换率的非劣效性未达到,但GMTs/GMCs依然强劲,表明该联合接种策略的整体免疫原性在本研究评估的年龄组中是得以保持的。 年龄分层分析揭示了预期的免疫衰老模式。老年人对SARS-CoV-2和流感的血清转换率较低,反映了与年龄相关的免疫功能下降。相比之下,对PPV23的应答在老年人中依然强劲,这与多糖抗原的T细胞非依赖性特性及其依赖既往积累的记忆B细胞池有关。 联合接种的安全性特征支持其实施。局部反应发生率略有增加,但主要为轻度和一过性;全身反应罕见。未发生与疫苗相关的SAEs。 content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, October 24, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Fungal Compound Sapinopyridione Shows Anti-SARS-CoV-2 Activity in Cells by October 23, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Fungal Compound Sapinopyridione Shows Anti-SARS-CoV-2 Activity in Cells Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A compound produced by an endophytic fungus isolated from Zanthoxylum piperitum shows potent activity against SARS-CoV-2 in infected cells, according to a study published in The Journal of Antibiotics on 23 October 2026. Shoji Maehara, Chiho Takahara, Ryo Watanabe, Serino Yoshitake, Toshiyuki Hata and colleagues, working with Shogo Nakajima, Hirofumi Ohashi and Koichi Watashi, isolated endophytic fungi from the plant and evaluated the anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity of their culture extracts. Of the 12 fungal isolates tested, six produced culture extracts that exhibited significant antiviral activity in SARS-CoV-2–infected cells. Three of these six active extracts also showed distinct inhibitory effects on the viral 3C-like (3CL) protease, indicating that the extracts act on a defined viral enzyme in addition to their broader antiviral activity in the cell-based assays. Chemical analysis of the active extracts identified sapinopyridione as the principal active metabolite. The compound is produced by a Botryosphaeria endophyte recovered from Zanthoxylum piperitum. In the infected-cell experiments, sapinopyridione displayed potent anti-SARS-CoV-2 activity, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 2.45 μM, equivalent to 0.58 μg/mL. The researchers report that this potency makes the compound a notable candidate among the metabolites recovered from the fungal collection. The study was motivated by the observation that endophytic fungi produce secondary metabolites that protect their host plants from external threats, a symbiotic system the authors describe as a promising source of antiviral compounds. Discover more Check Symptoms Save on Rx Biology textbook sales Learn Engineering Track Biotech By screening culture extracts rather than individual purified molecules from the outset, the team could link antiviral activity in infected cells to specific fungal isolates and then narrow down the responsible metabolite through chemical analysis. The authors conclude that sapinopyridione derivatives are promising lead compounds for the development of antiviral agents targeting SARS-CoV-2. The findings rest on cell-culture experiments with a limited set of 12 isolates from a single plant species, so they do not establish efficacy in humans. content_title: COVID-19 drugmaker Invivyd expands in New Haven as new CEO pursues broader drug market
content: Bioscience Health Care Real Estate & Construction Subscriber Only COVID-19 drugmaker Invivyd expands in New Haven as new CEO pursues broader drug market Invivyd Chairman and CEO Marc Elia at the company’s new headquarters at 205 Church St. in New Haven. The COVID-19 drugmaker more than doubled its office space as it prepares for potential growth. HBJ Photos | Steve Laschever By David Krechevsky October 20, 2026 Elia envisions a company several times its size, but Pemgarda’s June 2027 deadline puts $50 million-plus in yearly sales at risk. Already a Subscriber? Log in Get Instant Access to This Article Subscribe to Hartford Business Journal and get immediate access to all of our subscriber-only content and much more. Critical Hartford and Connecticut business news updated daily. Immediate access to all subscriber-only content on our website. Bi-weekly print or digital editions of our award-winning publication. Special bonus issues like the Hartford Book of Lists. Exclusive ticket prize draws for our in-person events. Click here to purchase a paywall bypass link for this article Biopharmaceutical company Invivyd Inc. only recently settled into its new, larger New Haven headquarters, but Chairman and CEO Marc Elia is already thinking about how to fill it. The company moved from about 13,600 square feet at 209 Church St. into 33,000 square feet at 205 Church St., more than doubling its space. The relocation comes as Invivyd develops a new COVID-19 prevention drug that it hopes will reach a broader market than its existing product. The company is also developing antibody drugs to prevent other infectious diseases. “Anticipated scale” drove the move, Elia said during a recent interview in the new headquarters. Invivyd has about 180 employees companywide, including those in Massachusetts and a national sales force. Elia said roughly 30 to 50 employees gather in New Haven on a given day. If Invivyd’s drug-development programs succeed, Elia said, he can envision the company growing to several times its current size over the next two to four years. But that growth depends on bringing new medicines to market as the company faces mounting losses and the June 2027 expiration of the emergency use authorization for its existing COVID-19 drug, Pemgarda. Invivyd develops drugs called monoclonal antibodies — laboratory-made proteins that help the body fight specific threats, such as viruses. Vaccines prompt the immune system to make antibodies; these drugs supply them directly. The company hopes its experimental COVID-19 prevention drug, VYD2311, will offer a broader alternative or complement to vaccination. It recently reported favorable results from a late-stage study examining the drug’s safety and how it works alongside a COVID-19 vaccine. Additional study results are expected to support its application for U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval. Elia, 50, added the CEO role in August after serving about four years as chairman. He became the company’s first permanent CEO since David Hering’s departure in April 2024. Elia said his transition to chief executive reflects his belief that Invivyd is approaching a turning point. “We’re on the precipice of really moving to ... achievement,” he said. “I’m incredibly passionate about what it is we do, how we do it, what good looks like and what sort of standards we need to enforce day to day.” Investor to CEO Much of Elia’s career has been spent as a healthcare investor, including as founder and chief investment officer of Stamford-based M28 Capital Management. Elia said that experience prepared him to lead Invivyd. His investment work focused largely on new medicines, requiring him to understand how diseases work and assess the science behind potential drugs. “I think of myself as a technologist first,” he said. Elia was involved with Invivyd from near its beginning and was already an investor in the company when he became ill with COVID-19. He later developed long COVID, a chronic condition that can occur after a COVID-19 infection and last at least three months. The experience did not initially draw him to Invivyd but strengthened his determination to advance new preventive options, he said. “For everything it has perhaps taken from me, it has added a measure of will,” he said. The company’s central premise is that its antibody drugs could be periodically updated to protect against new versions of viruses, much as vaccines are updated. “I think what we’re doing is we are creating a new category,” Elia said. Larger market potential Invivyd’s existing drug, Pemgarda, is authorized for emergency use to prevent COVID-19 in certain people with moderately to severely weakened immune systems. In June, however, the federal government announced that emergency use authorizations for COVID-19 drugs and biological products, including Pemgarda, will end June 29, 2027. Once the authorization ends, Invivyd will no longer be able to sell the drug unless it obtains FDA approval. Elia said Invivyd is working with regulators to avoid leaving patients without a preventive option. The issue also has significant financial implications for Invivyd. Pemgarda sales account for $50 million to $60 million in annual revenue, Elia said. The approaching authorization deadline creates a risk of a financial “cliff” if Invivyd cannot maintain sales of Pemgarda or bring its successor to market, he acknowledged. Invivyd hopes its experimental COVID-19 prevention drug, VYD2311, will serve a broader range of patients than Pemgarda. Elia estimated that 160 million to 170 million Americans are at increased risk of severe COVID-19, including people with obesity, diabetes or asthma. “We’re aiming at the biggest possible population,” he said. Reaching that market, however, depends on clinical results and FDA approval. In one Phase 3, or late-stage, trial, Invivyd evaluated VYD2311’s safety and whether giving it alongside a COVID-19 vaccine affected the immune system’s response to the vaccine. Elia said the results were favorable and showed no apparent interference with that response. A separate Phase 3 trial is examining the drug’s safety, antibody responses and ability to prevent symptomatic COVID-19. Invivyd plans to seek FDA approval through the agency’s accelerated approval program using safety and antibody response data from both studies. Under that plan, results measuring how well the drug prevents illness would follow if approval is granted. Meantime, Elia dismissed concerns that declining public attention to COVID-19 undermines the commercial opportunity. He compared the situation to HIV, which is no longer perceived as the public health emergency it once was but remains the basis for a large market for drugs that prevent infection or control the virus. “I haven’t met anyone who wants to get sick,” Elia said. Jodie Gillon, an infectious disease epidemiologist and president and CEO of BioCT, the state’s nonprofit bioscience trade organization, said Invivyd’s efforts are important and innovative. She said Invivyd’s recent expansion in New Haven is “another leap forward in Connecticut establishing itself as a world leader in life sciences with a history of COVID vaccine development right here.” Broader market Invivyd is also looking beyond COVID. The company is working on potential antibody drugs to prevent RSV, measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria and pertussis, Elia said. The resurgence of measles, he added, illustrates a potential role for the technology, including protecting people during outbreaks or complementing vaccination. The longer-term goal is to generate enough revenue from commercial products to finance development of those drugs without repeatedly turning to investors for capital, Elia said. Invivyd, though, remains unprofitable. As of June 30, it reported $160.1 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $226.7 million at the end of 2025. Product revenue rose to $28 million in the first six months of 2026, from $23.1 million a year earlier. Its net loss widened to $85.8 million from $30.9 million in the year-ago period. In its second-quarter filing, Invivyd said that, without additional financing, its available cash would not cover operating expenses and capital needs beyond a year from the report’s issuance in August. The company said it expects to fund operations through product revenue, financing and potential partnerships. Invivyd’s stock has also fallen sharply over the past year, losing more than half its value in the 12 months through early October. Shares were trading below $1, compared with about $1.63 a year earlier. Elia said he believes investors are awaiting “pivotal data” from the latest Phase 3 trial and the company’s next steps with the FDA, “and we are working hard to deliver against those milestones.” Elia’s employment agreement offers him a financial incentive for building the company’s value, including a transaction bonus if Invivyd is acquired for an equity value of at least $5 billion. Asked whether Invivyd’s ultimate goal is to be acquired, Elia said the objective is to create as much medical and shareholder value as possible. A sale, he said, would make sense only if a larger company could pursue Invivyd’s opportunity better or faster. “If at the end of the day someone wants to buy it, so be it,” Elia said. “But I think what we were trying to say to the world is, we’re here to make a big splash and create a huge amount of value.” Invivyd Inc. content_title: Needle-free mRNA vaccines protect mice against COVID-19 and flu
content: A needle-free vaccination method protected mice against the viruses that cause COVID-19 and flu, offering a possible new way to deliver mRNA vaccines while limiting unwanted inflammation. The Journal of Clinical Investigation study from researchers at Rutgers and the Japanese institutions tests experimental improvements to mRNA vaccine delivery. The approach combines a high-pressure liquid jet that delivers mRNA into the skin with two substances that strengthen the immune response. "Showing that a carrier-free, needle-free vaccine can be made protective opens a different design space than the one the field has been working in," said coauthor Renata Pasqualini of Rutgers New Jersey Medical School and Rutgers Cancer Institute, New Jersey's only National Cancer Institute-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center, together with RWJBarnabas Health. mRNA vaccines give cells temporary instructions to make a protein that trains the immune system to recognize a threat. In existing vaccines, tiny fat-based particles form capsules around the fragile mRNA, helping it enter cells and stimulate immunity. The researchers explored another approach: delivering unencapsulated, or "naked," mRNA into the skin, which is rich in immune cells. Earlier work showed that jet injection could effectively deliver mRNA, but the resulting immune response was weak. Researchers tried to bolster the effect by adding adjuvants, substances that enhance conventional vaccines. Unfortunately, these adjuvants offered little benefit when used individually with the mRNA. Some actually weakened parts of the response. However, combining two different adjuvants--aluminum phosphate and short DNA molecules called CpG--boosted both antibody and cellular responses. The researchers traced part of the benefit to immune signals activated in the skin and nearby lymph nodes. Their findings suggest that selecting the right immune stimulation and delivering mRNA into cells are essential to making this method work. One of the most exciting discoveries in developing our carrier-free mRNA vaccines was that a combination of adjuvants could markedly improve vaccine efficacy while maintaining a favorable safety profile in our animal studies." Satoshi Uchida, senior author, Institute of Science Tokyo After three doses, infectious virus was below detection limits in lung samples from mice given the boosted vaccines and later exposed to SARS-CoV-2 or influenza A. In the COVID-19 experiment, lung viral RNA was about 24 times lower than after vaccination without the adjuvants. Both flu vaccine groups survived, so no additional survival benefit from the boosters was established. Separate experiments found less local and systemic inflammation than with laboratory lipid-particle formulations of mRNA vaccine. Despite its success in mice, the new approach still needs testing in larger animals before human trials, including establishing suitable doses. "What encourages us is that we achieved protective immunity in mice with a delivery device and adjuvant components that have each already been clinically used in human patients," said coauthor Wadih Arap of Rutgers New Jersey Medical School and Rutgers Cancer Institute. Source: Journal reference: Qiao, N., et al . (2026). Jet-injected combinational adjuvants potentiate naked mRNA vaccines for protection against respiratory viral infections in mice. Journal of Clinical Investigation . DOI: 10.1172/jci204021. https://www.jci.org/articles/view/204021
